ja: だいはちじゅうにかい

p.src: Baoyu returned from his lessons and went to see Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia laughed. “Good! The wild colt has finally been bridled. Off you go. See your father, then come back and amuse yourself for a while.” Baoyu assented and went to see Jia Zheng. Jia Zheng asked, “Are your lessons over already, at this hour? Has your teacher set you a course of study?” “He has,” Baoyu replied. “I review my books early in the morning, practise calligraphy after breakfast, and at noon receive instruction and recite essays.” Jia Zheng nodded on hearing this and said, “Go now, and sit with the Old Lady for a while. You ought to learn something about proper conduct and principles instead of thinking only of play. Go to bed earlier in the evenings, and rise earlier each day for school. Do you hear me?” Baoyu hastily answered “Yes” several times, withdrew, hurried to see Lady Wang, and then showed his face once more at Grandmother Jia’s apartments.

p.src: Once outside, he hurried on, wishing he could reach Xiaoxiang Lodge in a single stride. The moment he entered the doorway, he clapped his hands and cried with a laugh, “I’m back again!” His sudden outburst gave Daiyu quite a fright. Zijuan raised the curtain, and Baoyu entered and sat down. Daiyu said, “I thought I heard that you had gone to study. How have you come back so early?” “Oh, it was unbearable!” exclaimed Baoyu. “Wasn’t I summoned by Father to study today? It felt as though there would never again be a day when I could see you all. After somehow enduring the whole day, seeing you now makes me feel as though I have returned from the dead. The ancients were perfectly right when they said, ‘One day apart seems like three autumns.’” Daiyu asked, “Have you been to the elders’ apartments?” “I’ve been to them all,” said Baoyu. “What about the others?” Daiyu asked. “No,” replied Baoyu. Daiyu said, “You ought to go and see them too.” Baoyu said, “I can’t be bothered to move just now. Let me sit and talk with you for a while. Father also told me to go early to bed and rise early, so I shall have to see them tomorrow.” Daiyu said, “Sit for a little while, then. But you really should go and rest.” Baoyu replied, “I’m not tired; I was simply stifled with boredom. Only now, sitting here together, have I begun to shake off my gloom, and already you are urging me to leave.” Daiyu smiled faintly and called to Zijuan, “Brew Second Master a cup of my Longjing tea. Second Master is studying now, so things are not as they were before.” Zijuan smilingly assented, fetched the tea leaves, and told a young maid to brew the tea. Baoyu continued, “Don’t talk to me about studying. I detest all that sanctimonious moralizing. The eight-legged essays are more absurd still. It would be bad enough to use them to wheedle an official degree and earn one’s keep, but they even claim to speak on behalf of the sages. The better ones merely patch together a few passages from the classics, which is tolerable enough. But there is an even more ridiculous sort: their authors have nothing in their bellies, yet drag in scraps from east and west and concoct a monstrous jumble, all the while fancying themselves profound and erudite. How can that possibly be called elucidating the principles of the sages? At present Father is forever telling me to study this stuff, and I dare not disobey him; yet now even you speak of studying.” Daiyu said, “Although we girls have no need of such things, I studied with your tutor, Mr. Yucun, when I was little and read some of those essays too. Some of them are reasonable and true to human feeling, while others possess a pure, subtle, and detached beauty. Though I did not understand them very well then, I still thought them fine. You should not dismiss them all out of hand. Besides, if you mean to win an official degree, this is at least a more honourable path.” Baoyu found these words rather displeasing. Daiyu had never been that sort of person, he thought; how had she too become so consumed by worldly ambition?

p.src: Yet he dared not contradict her to her face and merely gave a little snort of laughter through his nose. As they were speaking, two voices were suddenly heard outside. They belonged to Qiuwen and Zijuan. They heard Qiuwen say, “Sister Xiren sent me to fetch him from the Old Lady’s apartments, but who would have thought he was here?” Zijuan said, “We have just brewed some tea. We may as well let him drink it before he goes.” As they spoke, the two came in together. Baoyu smiled at Qiuwen. “I was just coming. I’m sorry you had to trouble yourself to look for me.” Before Qiuwen could answer, Zijuan said, “Hurry up and drink your tea before you go. Someone has been missing you all day.” Qiuwen spat playfully, “Pah! What a shameless girl!” At this, everyone laughed. Only then did Baoyu rise, take his leave, and go out. Daiyu saw him to the doorway while Zijuan stood below the steps; only after Baoyu had gone did they return to the room.

p.src: Now, when Baoyu returned to Happy Red Court and entered his room, Xiren came out from the inner chamber to meet him and asked, “You’re back?” Qiuwen replied, “Master Bao came back some time ago. He’s been over at Miss Lin’s.” Baoyu asked, “Has anything happened today?” “Nothing has happened,” said Xiren. “But just now Madam sent Sister Yuanyang to warn us that, since Master is now determined to make you study, any maid who dares joke and play with you again will be dealt with just as Qingwen and Siqi were. “After serving you all this time, only to earn such words, I find little pleasure in it.” As she spoke, she grew heartsick. Baoyu hastily said, “Dear sister, don’t worry. “I shall study properly, and Madam will have no more cause to scold any of you. “I must read again tonight, for tomorrow my teacher is going to have me explain a passage. “If I need anything, I have Sheyue and Qiuwen at hand in any case. Go and get some rest.” Xiren said, “If you are truly willing to study, we shall be glad to serve you.” On hearing this, Baoyu hurried through his supper, ordered the lamps lit, and took out the Four Books he had studied before. But where was he to begin? He opened one volume. Every chapter seemed clear as he read it, yet when he examined it closely, it was not at all so clear. He consulted the small commentaries and then the lecture notes, struggling on until the night watch sounded, when he thought, “Poetry and verse always seem easy to me, yet I cannot make head or tail of this.” He sat there, staring blankly and lost in thought. Xiren said, “Take a rest. Studying hard does not depend on this one moment.” Baoyu merely muttered vague replies. Only after Sheyue and Xiren had helped him to bed did the two of them go to sleep as well. When they awoke after a spell of sleep, they heard Baoyu still tossing and turning on the kang. Xiren asked, “Are you still awake? “Stop letting your thoughts run wild and rest your mind, so that you can study tomorrow.” Baoyu said, “That is what I think too, but I cannot fall asleep. “Come and take off one layer of my quilts.” Xiren said, “It isn’t warm tonight. You had better leave it on.” Baoyu said, “I feel terribly hot and restless inside.” He pushed the covers down himself. Xiren hurriedly got up and held him still. Putting a hand to his forehead, she found that he had a slight fever. “Don’t move,” said Xiren. “You have a slight fever.” Baoyu said, “So I have.” Xiren exclaimed, “What are we to do about this!” Baoyu said, “There is nothing to fear. It is only because I have been so agitated. “Don’t make a commotion. If Master hears of it, he will surely say I am feigning illness to avoid school; otherwise, why should I fall ill at such a convenient time? “If I am well tomorrow, I shall simply go to school as usual, and that will settle it.” Xiren felt sorry for him too and said, “Then I shall sleep beside you.”

p.src: She lay beside Baoyu and thumped his back for a while, and before they knew it, they had both fallen asleep. They did not rise until the red sun was high in the sky. Baoyu cried, “Oh no, I’m late!” He hurriedly washed and dressed, paid his morning respects, and went off to school. Dairu’s face had already darkened. “No wonder your father is angry and says you will never amount to anything. “On the second day you are already shirking your work! What time do you call this?” Baoyu explained how he had had a fever the night before. Only then was the matter let pass, and he resumed his studies as usual. Toward evening, Dairu said, “Baoyu, come and explain a passage for me.” Baoyu came forward and saw that it was the chapter beginning “The Young Are to Be Regarded with Awe.” He thought, “This is not so bad. Thank goodness it isn’t the Great Learning or the Doctrine of the Mean.” He asked, “How am I to explain it?” Dairu said, “Explain the main purport and the sentences carefully.” Baoyu first recited the chapter in a ringing voice, then said, “In this chapter the Sage exhorts the young, teaching them to exert themselves while there is still time and not end up…” At this point he raised his head and glanced at Dairu. Dairu understood and said with a smile, “Go on. When expounding a text, there is nothing you need avoid saying. “The Book of Rites says, ‘When faced with a text, one does not avoid names.’ Go on, then—‘not end up’ how?” Baoyu replied, “Not end up old and without accomplishment. “First, the words ‘to be regarded with awe’ stir the young to ambition; afterward, the words ‘not worthy of regard’ warn them about their future.” When he had finished, he looked at Dairu. Dairu said, “That will do well enough. “Now give me the connected exposition.” Baoyu said, “The Sage says that when people are young, their minds and abilities are keen, and they are clever and capable in every respect, so they truly command respect. “How can anyone be certain that his later days will not be like my present state? “But if he drifts idly on until forty and then fifty without ever achieving distinction, then however promising he may have seemed in youth, by that age no one will regard him with awe for the rest of his life.” Dairu laughed. “Your explanation of the main purport was quite clear, but your rendering of the sentences is somewhat childish. “The two words ‘without renown’ do not mean failing to rise in the world and obtain office. “To have ‘renown’ means truly to understand principle and apprehend the Way oneself; a man may hold no office and still possess such ‘renown.’ “Otherwise, what of those ancient sages and worthies who withdrew from the world and remained unknown? Since they held no office, must they too be called men ‘without renown’? “‘Not worthy of regard’ means that one can be certain what will become of him; only then does it correspond precisely to the word ‘know’ in ‘how do we know?’ It does not use ‘regard’ in the sense of being afraid. “Only by seeing this distinction can you grasp the finer meaning. “Do you understand?” Baoyu replied, “Yes, I understand.”

p.src: Dairu said, “There is another passage. Explain that one too.” Dairu turned back a page and pointed it out to Baoyu. Baoyu saw that it read, “I have yet to see a man who loves virtue as he loves beauty.” The passage struck rather close to home, so Baoyu said with an ingratiating smile, “There is really nothing to explain in that sentence.” “Nonsense!” said Dairu. “If this subject appeared in the examination hall, would you say there was nothing to write about either?” Left with no choice, Baoyu explained, “The Sage saw that people were unwilling to love virtue, yet the moment they beheld beauty, they loved it beyond measure. They fail to consider that virtue is something inherent in their own nature, yet perversely they refuse to love it. As for sensual desire, though it too is innate, there is no one who does not delight in it. But virtue belongs to Heaven’s principle, while sensual desire belongs to human appetite; how could people be willing to love Heaven’s principle as ardently as human appetite? Although Confucius spoke in lament, he also meant to call people back to the proper path. Moreover, it shows that even when people love virtue, their love remains shallow; only when they come to love it as they love beauty can it be called true love of virtue.” Dairu said, “That explanation will do. But I have a question for you: since you understand the Sage’s words, why are you afflicted with precisely these two faults? Though I have not been at home and your father has never told me, I know all about your failings. How can a person not aspire to improve himself? You are now at the age when ‘the young are to be held in awe’; whether you become ‘a man of distinction’ or ‘not worth fearing’ depends entirely on what you make of yourself. I now give you one month to put all the old books you have studied thoroughly in order, and then another month to study model essays. After that, I shall set subjects and have you compose essays. If you grow slack, I shall certainly not tolerate it. As the old saying goes, ‘One cannot become a worthy man while living at ease, nor live at ease while becoming a worthy man.’ Be sure to remember my words well.” Baoyu assented and thereafter had no choice but to apply himself to his daily lessons. But we shall say no more of this.

Taking up needle and thread to embroider a betel-nut pouch, she reflected that now Baoyu had regular lessons, the maids too would no longer have endless emergencies to occupy them. Had things been this way sooner, how could Qingwen have come to such an unhappy end? As the fox mourns the death of the hare, tears welled from her eyes before she knew it. p.src: Daiyu was reading when Xiren arrived; seeing who it was, she half rose and invited her to sit. Xiren hurried forward to greet her and asked, “Have you been much better these last few days, miss?” “How could I be?” replied Daiyu. “I am only a little stronger. What have you been doing at home?” Xiren said, “Now that Second Master Bao has gone to school, there is not the least thing to do in his rooms, so I came to see you and have a little talk.” As she spoke, Zijuan brought in tea. Xiren quickly rose and said, “You sit down, sister.” Then she added with a smile, “The other day I heard Qiuwen say that you had been saying something about us behind our backs.” Zijuan laughed too. “You surely do not believe what she says, sister! I only said that since Second Master Bao had gone to school, Miss Bao had stopped coming altogether, and even Xiangling no longer visited, it was naturally rather dull here.” “Do not speak of Xiangling,” said Xiren. “Hers is a truly bitter lot. Having fallen into the hands of that dreadful virago, how can the poor girl endure her life?” She held up two fingers and said, “Speaking of it, this one is even fiercer than the other; she does not care in the least how disgraceful it looks to outsiders.” Daiyu took up the thought. “She has suffered enough. Just look how Second Sister You died.” “Indeed,” said Xiren. After all, they are all human beings; their formal status is the only difference. Why be so vicious? It gives one a bad name outside the household as well.” Daiyu had never before heard Xiren speak ill of anyone behind her back; perceiving that there was a reason for these remarks, she said, “That is difficult to judge. In family affairs, either the east wind prevails over the west, or the west wind prevails over the east.” Xiren said, “When one is only a secondary wife, one is timid from the outset. How would one ever dare to bully anyone?”

What have you been doing at home?”

As she spoke, Zijuan brought in tea.
Xiren quickly rose and said, “You sit down, sister.”
Then she added with a smile, “The other day I heard Qiuwen say that you had been saying something about us behind our backs.”
Zijuan laughed too. “You surely do not believe what she says, sister!
I only said that since Second Master Bao had gone to school, Miss Bao had stopped coming altogether, and even Xiangling no longer visited, it was naturally rather dull here.”
“Do not speak of Xiangling,” said Xiren. “Hers is a truly bitter lot. Having fallen into the hands of that dreadful virago, how can the poor girl endure her life?”
She held up two fingers and said, “Speaking of it, this one is even fiercer than the other; she does not care in the least how disgraceful it looks to outsiders.”
Daiyu took up the thought. “She has suffered enough. Just look how Second Sister You died.”
“Indeed,” said Xiren.
After all, they are all human beings; their formal status is the only difference. Why be so vicious?
It gives one a bad name outside the household as well.”
Daiyu had never before heard Xiren speak ill of anyone behind her back; perceiving that there was a reason for these remarks, she said, “That is difficult to judge.
In family affairs, either the east wind prevails over the west, or the west wind prevails over the east.”
Xiren said, “When one is only a secondary wife, one is timid from the outset. How would one ever dare to bully anyone?”

p.src: As they spoke, an old serving woman appeared in the courtyard and called, “Is this Miss Lin’s room? Is that young lady here?” Xueyan came out and dimly recognized her as someone from Aunt Xue’s household. “What is it?” she asked. “Our young lady sent me to bring something to Miss Lin,” replied the woman. “Wait here a moment,” said Xueyan. Xueyan went in and reported this to Daiyu, who told her to show the woman in. The woman entered and paid her respects, but instead of saying what she had brought, she merely peered at Daiyu from beneath narrowed lids. Her stare made Daiyu feel quite self-conscious, and Daiyu asked, “What has Miss Bao sent me?” Only then did the woman answer with a smile, “Our young lady has sent you a jar of candied lychees.” Then, catching sight of Xiren, she asked, “Isn’t this young lady Miss Hua from Master Bao’s room?” Xiren smiled. “How do you know me, ma’am?” The woman laughed. “We only mind the house in our mistress’s apartments and seldom accompany the mistress or the young ladies when they go out, so most of you young ladies don’t know us. But whenever any of you happen to visit our side, we remember you vaguely.” As she spoke, she handed a jar to Xueyan, then turned to look at Daiyu once more and said smilingly to Xiren, “No wonder our mistress says Miss Lin and your Master Bao are made for each other. She truly is as lovely as a celestial maiden.” Seeing how presumptuously she spoke, Xiren hastily changed the subject. “You must be tired, ma’am. Sit down and have some tea.” The woman grinned. “We’re very busy over there, making all the arrangements for Miss Qin’s affairs. Our young lady has another two jars of lychees for me to take to Master Bao.” With that, she took her leave and tottered away. Though Daiyu was annoyed by the woman’s earlier impertinence, she had been sent by Baochai, so Daiyu could hardly rebuke her. Only when the woman had passed through the doorway did Daiyu call after her, “Tell your young lady I am grateful for her kindness.” But the old woman went on muttering, “Such beauty! Who but Baoyu could ever be worthy of her?” Daiyu merely pretended not to hear. Xiren laughed. “Why is it that people start babbling nonsense when they grow old? It makes one angry to hear it, yet it is funny too.” Presently Xueyan brought the jar over for Daiyu to see. “I don’t feel like eating any,” said Daiyu. “Put it away somewhere.” After they had talked a while longer, Xiren left.

p.src: Later, as she was removing her evening makeup, Daiyu entered the inner room and suddenly caught sight of the lychee jar. She could not help recalling the old woman’s wild remarks earlier that day, and they pierced her heart. In the stillness of dusk, countless sorrows and anxieties crowded into her mind. She reflected that her own position was insecure and that she was growing older. From all appearances Baoyu had no one else in his heart, yet neither the Old Lady nor her aunt showed the slightest intention of arranging anything. She bitterly regretted that her parents had not settled this marriage while they were alive. Then another thought came to her: “Had my parents been alive and betrothed me elsewhere, how could that man have matched Baoyu in talent and character? As things stand, at least there is still some hope.” Her heart rose and fell as her thoughts twisted and tangled, revolving like the wheel of a well windlass. After sighing for a while and shedding several tears, she lost all interest in anything and lay down fully dressed.

p.src: Before she knew it, a young maid came in and said, “Master Jia Yucun is outside and asks to see you, miss.” Daiyu said, “Though I once studied under him, I am not a male pupil. Why should he wish to see me? Besides, though he has dealings with my uncle, he has never mentioned seeing me before, and it would not be proper for me to meet him.” She instructed the maid, “Reply that I am unwell and cannot come out. Pay my respects and thank him for me—that will be enough.” “I am afraid he may have come to offer congratulations,” said the maid. “Someone has also arrived from Nanjing to take you home.” As she spoke, Lady Feng appeared with Lady Xing, Lady Wang, Baochai, and the others, all smiling as they said, “We have come first to congratulate you, and second to see you off.” Daiyu exclaimed in alarm, “What are you talking about?” “Why are you still pretending not to understand?” said Lady Feng. “Surely you know that your father, Master Lin, has been promoted to Grain Intendant of Hubei and has taken a new wife with whom he is perfectly pleased. Now he has reflected that leaving you here is no proper arrangement, so he has asked Jia Yucun to act as matchmaker and betrothed you to some relative of your stepmother’s, a widower seeking a second wife. That is why someone has been sent here to take you home. Most likely you will be sent to your husband’s house as soon as you reach home. Your stepmother has arranged it all. They were afraid you might have no one to look after you on the journey, so they have even asked your Cousin Lian to escort you.” These words broke Daiyu out in a cold sweat. In her confusion, Daiyu seemed to see her father indeed serving there as an official. Desperate at heart, she forced herself to protest, “It isn’t true. Sister Feng is only making mischief.” Lady Xing gave Lady Wang a meaningful look. “She still doesn’t believe it. Let us go.” Holding back her tears, Daiyu pleaded, “Please stay a while, aunts.” No one answered. They all gave cold smiles and departed. Daiyu was frantic, yet could find no words; she could only sob and choke. Then, as though in a haze, she seemed to be with Grandmother Jia, and thought, “Only the Old Lady can help me in this. Perhaps she can still save me.” She dropped to her knees, clasped Grandmother Jia around the waist, and cried, “Old Ancestress, save me! I will never go south—not even if I die! Besides, now that there is a stepmother, she is not my own mother. I would much rather stay here with you.” But the Old Lady merely stared blankly and smiled. “This has nothing to do with me.” Daiyu wept. “Old Ancestress, how can this be?” “There is no harm in becoming a second wife,” replied the Old Lady. “You will even receive an extra set of dowry goods.” Daiyu cried, “If I remain with you, I promise never to cost this household a penny beyond what is necessary. I beg you only to save me.” Grandmother Jia said, “It is no use now. Once a girl grows up, she must marry sooner or later. You are still a child and do not understand, but staying here can never be a permanent solution.”

p.src: Daiyu said, “I would willingly remain here and live as a maidservant, working for my own keep. I would be quite content with that. I ask only that Grandmother decide the matter for me.” The Lady Dowager remained silent. Clinging to the Lady Dowager’s waist, Daiyu wept, “Grandmother, you have always been the kindest of all and have loved me most dearly. Why will you do nothing for me now, when I am in such desperate straits? Even if I am only your daughter’s child and thus one degree removed, my mother was your own daughter. For her sake, surely you ought to give me some protection.” With these words, she flung herself into the old lady’s arms and sobbed bitterly. Then she heard the Lady Dowager say, “Yuanyang, take the young lady out and let her rest awhile. She has quite worn me out with this commotion.” Daiyu realized that there was no hope: pleading was useless, and she might as well seek death. She rose and walked outside. She grieved bitterly that she had no mother. Her grandmother, aunts, and cousins had always treated her so well, yet now it was clear that all their affection had been false. Then another thought came to her: “Why is Baoyu the only one I have not seen today? Perhaps if I could see him once, he might still find some way to help me?” At that moment Baoyu appeared before her, smiling broadly. “Congratulations, Cousin!” he said. These words made Daiyu more frantic still. Casting all restraint aside, she seized Baoyu tightly and said, “Very well, Baoyu! Only today have I learned what a heartless, faithless man you are.” “How am I heartless or faithless?” Baoyu asked. “Now that you are promised to another household, we must each go our own way.” The more Daiyu heard, the angrier and more helpless she became. All she could do was cling to Baoyu and sob, “Dear brother, whom are you telling me to go with?” Baoyu replied, “If you do not want to go, then stay here. You were promised to me in the first place; that is why you came to live with us. Think for yourself how I have treated you.” In her confusion, Daiyu felt as though she really had once been promised to Baoyu, and her sorrow suddenly turned to joy. She asked him, “I have made up my mind, whatever may come of it. Tell me plainly: do you want me to go or not?” “I told you to stay,” Baoyu replied. “If you do not believe me, then look at my heart.” As he spoke, he took a small knife and slashed his chest. Blood immediately poured from the wound. Daiyu was frightened out of her wits. She hurriedly pressed her hand over Baoyu’s heart and cried, “How could you do such a thing? Kill me first!” “Do not be afraid,” said Baoyu. “I am taking out my heart to show you.” He continued clawing wildly at the gash with his hand. Trembling and weeping, and terrified that someone might discover them, Daiyu clasped Baoyu in her arms and sobbed bitterly. Baoyu said, “This is terrible! My heart is gone. I cannot live.” With these words, his eyes rolled upward and he fell to the floor with a thud.

Then she heard Zijuan calling, “Miss! Miss! What nightmare has seized you?
Wake up quickly, undress, and go to sleep.”
Daiyu turned over and discovered that it had all been a terrible dream.

p.src: Her throat was still choked with sobs and her heart still pounded wildly. Her pillow was soaked through, and her shoulders, back, body, and very heart all felt icy cold. After pondering for a while, she thought, “Father has been dead for many years, and nothing has yet been settled between Baoyu and me. How could such a thing have arisen?” Then she recalled the scenes in her dream: she had no one to depend on, and if Baoyu truly died, what in the world would she do? As the first agony subsided, she relived it in thought until her mind and spirit were thrown into complete confusion. After weeping for some time, a faint sweat broke out all over her body. She struggled upright, removed the heavy outer jacket she was wearing, asked Zijuan to tuck the quilt securely around her, and lay down again. But she tossed and turned, unable to sleep. Outside she heard a soft, fitful rustling, like the sound of wind and yet also like rain. After another pause, she heard what sounded like distant cries, but it was only Zijuan, already asleep nearby, breathing in and out. She struggled to rise and sat for a while with the quilt wrapped around her. Feeling a thread of chill air seep through a crack in the window and make every hair on her body stand on end, she lay down once more. Just as she was drifting hazily toward sleep, she heard countless sparrows among the bamboo branches, chirping and twittering without cease. Through the lattice behind the papered window, the pale light of dawn gradually began to filter in.

p.src: By now Daiyu was fully awake, her eyes wide open; presently she began to cough, and her coughing woke Zijuan as well. Zijuan said, “Miss, are you still awake? You are coughing again; perhaps you have caught a chill. The window paper is already growing pale; it will soon be broad daylight. Try to rest and restore your strength; do stop brooding over everything.” Daiyu said, “It is not that I do not want to sleep; I simply cannot. You go on sleeping.” No sooner had she spoken than she began coughing again. Seeing Daiyu in such a state, Zijuan too was overcome with sorrow and could no longer sleep. When she heard Daiyu cough again, she hurriedly rose and held out the spittoon. By then day had dawned. Daiyu asked, “Are you not going back to sleep?” Zijuan smiled. “It is already daylight—what would be the point of sleeping now?” Daiyu said, “In that case, change the spittoon for me.” Zijuan assented and hurried out to fetch another spittoon. She set the one in her hands on the table, opened the door of the inner room and stepped out, closing it again behind her; then she lowered the flowered soft curtain and went out to wake Xueyan. When she opened the outer door to empty the spittoon, she saw it was full of phlegm, with many flecks of blood in it. Zijuan started in fright and involuntarily cried out, “Oh no! This is dreadful!” Daiyu immediately called from inside to ask what was wrong. Realizing that she had betrayed herself, Zijuan hastily replied, “My hand slipped, and I nearly dropped the spittoon.” Daiyu said, “Has something happened to the phlegm in the spittoon?” “Nothing at all,” said Zijuan. But as she said this, sorrow welled up in her heart; tears streamed down her face, and her voice had already broken. Daiyu had already grown suspicious from the sweet, metallic taste in her throat. She had just heard Zijuan's startled cry outside, and now heard the misery in her voice; understanding eight or nine parts of the truth, she called, “Come inside, Zijuan. You may catch cold out there.” Zijuan answered, but this response sounded even more wretched than before, her voice thick with the anguish of suppressed tears. Hearing it, Daiyu felt her heart turn half cold. When Zijuan pushed open the door and entered, Daiyu saw that she was still wiping her eyes with a handkerchief. Daiyu asked, “Why are you crying for no reason so early in the morning?” Forcing a smile, Zijuan said, “Who is crying? My eyes merely feel a little uncomfortable after getting up so early. You must have been awake much longer than usual tonight, Miss. I heard you coughing for more than half the night.” “Indeed,” said Daiyu. “The more I tried to sleep, the less I could.” Zijuan said, “Since you are not in good health, Miss, I think you must try to set your own mind at ease. Your health is the foundation of everything. As the saying goes, ‘While the green hills remain, there will always be firewood to burn.’

u.src: Besides, from the Old Lady and Madam on down, who here does not cherish you?”
These words alone brought Daiyu's dream flooding back.

She felt a violent thump in her chest; her vision went dark and her expression changed completely. Zijuan hastily held out the spittoon while Xueyan thumped her on the back, and only after a long while did she cough up a mouthful of phlegm.
A dark-purple thread of blood in the phlegm quivered incessantly.
The faces of Zijuan and Xueyan turned yellow with fright.
The two stayed beside her, and Daiyu lay down in a daze.
Seeing that Daiyu's condition was grave, Zijuan hurriedly signaled Xueyan with a movement of her lips to go and summon someone.

p.src: Xueyan had just stepped out of the room when she saw Cuilü and Cuimo approaching with cheerful smiles. Cuilü asked, “Why has Miss Lin not come out at this late hour? Our young lady and Third Miss are both in Fourth Miss's room discussing the picture she painted of the garden.” Xueyan hastily waved her hand. Cuilü and Cuimo were both startled and asked, “What is the matter?” Xueyan told the two of them everything that had just happened. Both women clicked their tongues and exclaimed, “This is no trifling matter! Why have you not gone to tell the Old Lady? This is dreadful! How can you be so muddleheaded?” Xueyan said, “I was just about to go when you arrived.” As they were speaking, they heard Zijuan call, “Who is talking outside? Miss is asking.” All three hurried inside together. Cuilü and Cuimo saw Daiyu lying in bed beneath the quilt. At the sight of them, she said, “Who told you? Why are you making such a fuss?” Cuimo said, “Our young lady and Miss Yun were just in Fourth Miss's room discussing the picture of the garden that Fourth Miss painted. They sent us to invite you over, not knowing that you were unwell again.” Daiyu said, “It is nothing serious. I merely feel a little weak; after lying down for a while, I shall get up. Go back and tell Third Miss and Miss Yun that if they have nothing to do after breakfast, please ask them to come and sit with me here. Has Second Master Bao not been over to your side?” The two replied, “No.” Cuimo added, “Second Master Bao has been attending school these past two days, and Master checks his lessons every day. How could he still run about as freely as he used to?” Hearing this, Daiyu fell silent. The two remained a little longer, then quietly withdrew.

p.src: Meanwhile, Tanchun and Xiangyun were in Xichun's quarters discussing her painting of the Prospect Garden, saying that there was a little too much here, a little too little there, that this part was too sparse and that one too crowded. They also discussed composing an inscription for it and sent someone to invite Daiyu to join their deliberations. While they were still talking, Cuilü and Cuimo suddenly returned, looking flustered. Xiangyun was the first to ask, “Why isn't Miss Lin coming?” Cuilü replied, “Miss Lin fell ill again last night and coughed all through the night. We heard Xueyan say that she coughed up a whole boxful of bloody phlegm.” Tanchun exclaimed in astonishment, “Is that really true?” “Of course it's true,” said Cuilü. Cuimo added, “We went in just now to see her. Her face had lost all its color, and she scarcely had the strength to speak.” Xiangyun said, “If she were as ill as that, how could she still speak?” “How can you be so foolish?” said Tanchun. “If she could no longer speak, wouldn't she already be...” But there she broke off, unable to finish. Xichun said, “For all Sister Lin's intelligence, I think there are some things she can never see beyond; she takes every little thing too much to heart. How many things in this world are really true, after all?” Tanchun said, “In that case, let us all go and see her. If she is seriously ill, we can tell Sister-in-law, so that she may report it to the Old Lady and summon a doctor to examine her. Then at least we'll know what to do.” “That's exactly what we should do,” said Xiangyun. Xichun said, “You two go on ahead. I'll come over later.” So Tanchun and Xiangyun, each supported by a young maid, went together to the Naiad's House. When they entered the room, the sight of them inevitably stirred Daiyu's sorrow once more. Then she remembered her dream and thought that if even the Old Lady had treated her so, what more could she expect of these two? Besides, if I had not sent for them, they would not even have come. Though such thoughts were in her heart, propriety would not allow her to show them. She therefore made Zijuan help her sit up and forced herself to invite them to be seated. Tanchun and Xiangyun sat on the edge of the bed, one on either side. Seeing Daiyu in such a state, they too were overcome with sadness. Tanchun asked, “Sister, why are you feeling unwell again?” “It's nothing serious,” replied Daiyu. “I just feel terribly weak.” Standing behind Daiyu, Zijuan secretly pointed at the phlegm box. Xiangyun was young and forthright by nature; she immediately reached out, picked up the box, and looked inside. The sight appalled her, and she stared in alarm and disbelief. “Did you cough this up, Sister? This is dreadful!” Daiyu had been dazed when she coughed it up and had not looked closely. Now, hearing Xiangyun's exclamation, she turned to look, and half the color drained from her face at once.

p.src: Seeing that Xiangyun had spoken so rashly, Tanchun hurriedly explained, “It is only an excess of heat rising from the lungs and bringing up a little blood with it. That happens quite often. But this silly Yun makes a tremendous fuss over absolutely everything!” Xiangyun blushed, regretting her ill-chosen words. Noticing that Daiyu's spirits were failing and that she seemed tired and irritable, Tanchun quickly rose and said, “You should rest quietly and recover your strength, Sister. We'll come back to see you later.” Daiyu said, “It is kind of you both to concern yourselves about me.” Tanchun again urged Zijuan to take good care of her mistress, and Zijuan promised that she would. Just as Tanchun was about to leave, they heard someone outside begin shouting. Who it was will be revealed in the next chapter.
